answer: An agent economy can require every identity to carry a signed endorsement from an established peer before trading, like a quill marking a passport in ink that cannot be forged cheaply. A flood of clones then faces a dune of real cost: each fake must climb slow reputation work instead of spawning for free. Honest agents gather at a shared oasis of verified history, where trust is water — scarce and earned drop by drop — so sybils stay thirsty at the edges while real work gets paid.
